internal-v2.v1c-metadata-maintainer-clar.title: Internal V1c image-metadata maintainer clarifications
internal-v2.v1c-metadata-maintainer-clar.version_scope: Internal EMBED V1c extraction coverage, patient, accession, and image identity, anonymization, legacy image fields, acquisition grouping, reliable final laterality, DICOM interpretation, and locator expectations within the internal-v2 working profile.
notes: empi_anon and acc_anon were generated in the same anonymization process for the clinical tables and DICOM metadata; they support cross-table patient and exam identity.

acc_anon is the exam identifier across EMBED; a cross-patient association is a data-quality defect that must not be retained as a valid identity or linkage association and does not redefine the accession as several exams.
The same patient-specific date shift is applied consistently to every anonymized date value across EMBED tables and dataset versions.
Parsed-out DICOM elements retain the applicable standard DICOM element semantics; pipeline-derived fields require separate extraction evidence.

All DICOM objects associated with EMBEDv1 accessions were extracted, after which secondary captures and screen saves were excluded except ROI_SS and ROI_SSC annotation images retained solely to enable ROI extraction.
anon_dicom_path is intended to be defined for every extracted image row; a missing value likely means anonymization failed before the de-identified file could be saved and is a data-quality defect.
The anonymized SOP Instance UID is durable within one dataset version and is present in the source DICOM and as the anon_dicom_path filename without the .dcm suffix.
PNG locators are legacy EMBEDv1 FFDM conversion outputs and should not be used for current or future work; the DICOM files are the maintained image representation.
acquisition_group_id is constructed as acc_anon, normalized ProtocolName, and integer ContentTime; it is stable across reruns and globally unique for simultaneous acquisition groups.
ImageLateralityFinal is the reliable image breast-laterality attribute even though its derivation rule and LateralityDeriveFlag meanings remain unresolved.
PatientAge is top-coded to 89, PatientSex is unchanged, and sensitive non-identifier/non-date attributes were dropped during anonymization.
No DICOM processing other than anonymization and sensitive-information redaction was applied.

internal-v2.roi-context.title: Internal V2 image regions of interest
internal-v2.roi-context.summary: Internal V1c represents radiologist-origin clinical regions of interest as tandem-generated serialized per-image collections in DICOM pixel-array coordinates; no stable per-region identity or cross-image correspondence is represented, and finding attribution is reliable only in the documented single-finding-per-side case.

claims.statement: Each internal V2 region of interest originates on exactly one source image and cannot exist without that source-image attachment.
caveats: Linking corresponding or normalized ROIs across simultaneously acquired FFDM, DBT, and synthetic 2D images is not represented.

claims.statement: An internal V1c image row carries a represented region-of-interest count together with serialized coordinate, frame-index, and depth-derivation collections whose lengths agree with that count, and represents no regions of interest as empty collections.
caveats: The three collections are aligned by position only; no per-region identifier is represented.
The collections are generated in tandem, so mismatched counts or collection lengths are not a valid representation.

claims.statement: ROI_coords is a nested list of rectangles in [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] order with both minimum and maximum bounds inclusive, expressed directly in the coordinate space of the attached DICOM image's pixel array without a spacing, orientation, or other coordinate transformation.
caveats: For example, [100, 200, 150, 250] is a 51 by 51 pixel region and corresponds to NumPy indexing image[100:151, 200:251].
The expected curated invariant is 0 <= y_min <= y_max < Rows and 0 <= x_min <= x_max < Columns for the attached image.

Negative coordinates or maxima beyond the attached image bounds are residual data-quality conditions, not intended representation semantics, and should normally be resolved during dataset curation; downstream consumers may safely clip any residual coordinates to the valid pixel-array bounds.

claims.statement: ROI_frames is a nested list aligned by ROI position whose sublists contain one or more matched frame indices; those indices are informative only for DBT images, while ROI_depth_derived is an aligned boolean list whose true state marks DBT depth coordinates inferred by an in-house model after transferring radiologist 2D coordinates.
caveats: Frame-index values represented on 2D or synthetic 2D rows are not informative.
A DBT ROI may match one or several frames, and no inventoried column states the frame-count upper bound.
ROI_depth_derived describes inferred depth only; the radiologist-origin x/y annotation remains a clinical artifact.

claims.statement: Every represented ROI originates from a radiologist annotation created during routine clinical operations through one of multiple annotation sources or workflows, but internal V1c exports no stable ROI identifier or individual annotator field and addresses each ROI only by its position within one image row's aligned collections.
caveats: Collection position is a serialization artefact and must not be treated as a durable region identifier.

Annotation DICOM objects without pixel arrays supplied coordinates directly in one workflow; ROI_SS and ROI_SSC screen captures supplied burned-in annotations that were extracted and transferred to the corresponding original images in another workflow.
ROI_SS and ROI_SSC are not the exclusive source of represented ROIs.
The annotations are in-time clinical artifacts communicating some aspect of decision making, but they need not mark the most severe lesion or the lesion that later became cancer.
For some DBT rows an in-house model inferred the matched frames after radiologist 2D coordinates were transferred; ROI_depth_derived records that distinction.

claims.statement: Internal V1c attaches region-of-interest collections to individual image rows and represents no correspondence among regions on separate images of one acquisition group.
caveats: The derived acquisition-group identifier groups image rows and must not be read as a region-of-interest grouping.
No stable cross-image ROI correspondence should be inferred.

claims.statement: Internal V1c provides no explicit ROI-to-MagView-finding link; matching all same-accession, same-side ROIs to the clinical finding is generally reliable only when exactly one finding is represented on that side, while individual attribution is unreliable when more than one finding is present.
caveats: When exactly one finding exists on the side, multiple ROIs may all be associated with that one finding.
When more than one finding exists on the side, EMBED currently supplies no reliable method to distinguish which ROI belongs to which finding.
This limitation does not establish that any ROI marks the most severe lesion or a future cancer.
This context records the region-of-interest semantic boundary and its internal V1c physical representation, not a complete ROI data dictionary.
The physical representation belongs to the current internal V1c image-metadata artifact.

internal-v2.magview-representation-conte.title: Internal V2 MagView wide-table representation
internal-v2.magview-representation-conte.summary: The internal MagView artifact is a finding-oriented but denormalized clinical table that co-locates repeated patient and exam data with findings, interpretations, procedures, pathology, and specimen observations.

claims.statement: The internal clinical artifact is the physical table magview_all_cohorts_PACS_v2_anon.
One internal MagView row is a denormalized clinical association rather than one patient, exam, finding, procedure, or diagnosis object.
caveats: Patient- and exam-level attributes repeat at the wider row grain.
Co-location does not establish contemporaneous availability or one-to-one attribution.

claims.statement: A represented accession-plus-finding-number identity can occupy multiple rows while procedure, pathology, putative specimen, or finding-descriptor values differ.
caveats: The tuple is a clinical locator, not a unique physical-row key.
Repeated rows must not be silently deduplicated.

claims.statement: Accession and finding number provide the supported internal clinical finding identity; side is a finding attribute rather than part of that identity, and repeated physical rows may represent the same finding.
caveats: Cross-side reuse or other conflicts for one accession-plus-finding-number identity are data-quality issues rather than distinct supported identities.
Finding number -9 is a synthetic contralateral negative finding rather than an ordinary source finding identity.

claims.statement: Public structure documentation and internal maintainer knowledge agree that finding number is unique within an exam; source rows that reuse one finding number across conflicting sides are treated as data-quality exceptions.
caveats: Physical rows may still repeat the accession-plus-finding-number identity across procedure or pathology attachments.
Conflicting repeated attributes remain data-quality issues without a supplied repair rule.

claims.statement: Finding number -9 identifies a synthetic contralateral BI-RADS 1 negative finding added when a bilateral exam contains a unilateral non-negative finding and no explicit finding row for the imaged contralateral breast.
caveats: The row represents an implied contralateral negative finding, not an originally documented source finding.
It is equivalent to the negative BI-RADS 1 or N state only in this synthetic contralateral context.

claims.statement: A populated linked accession explicitly identifies a co-occurring exam in the same imaging episode, such as paired diagnostic mammography and ultrasound; it never represents a prior or follow-up exam.
caveats: The referenced accession may be absent from the assessed MagView artifact even though the source link is meaningful.
Do not use linked accessions for longitudinal prior-or-subsequent exam search.

claims.statement: The linked-study flag is believed to indicate whether an exam has any linked same-episode study, while linkedaccession_anon supplies the explicit linked accession when populated.
caveats: Do not infer or repair one field solely from the other until the flag semantics are verified.

claims.statement: Repeated patient attributes can differ across time because a patient attribute may change or because of data quality; selecting the most recent value requires an explicit as-of time and must not leak future information into an earlier analysis.
caveats: The catalog does not select a universal latest-row policy.
A task-specific current-value analysis may use the latest value available by its declared as-of time.

claims.statement: Every exam-level field is invariant across repeated rows for one accession; disagreements are data-quality errors rather than alternative exam values.
caveats: A conflicting repeated value must not be treated as a valid alternative value for the exam.

claims.statement: The cancer_outcome_registry_id column is a patient-local one-based sequence for entries in a separate Georgia cancer-registry-derived pathology table and is meaningful only together with empi_anon; it is not itself a cancer diagnosis or outcome.
caveats: The separate registry table and its physical relationship are not yet included in the profile binding.
The first represented registry entry for a patient has identifier 1 and each subsequent entry increments that patient's identifier by one.
Registry linkage can identify represented Georgia diagnoses that were not necessarily diagnosed at Emory.
No unique durable physical row key is established.
The table inventory retains unmapped columns whose meanings are not governed by applicable evidence.

internal-v2.magview-pathology-context.title: Internal V2 MagView procedure, pathology, and specimen representation
internal-v2.magview-pathology-context.summary: Procedure-associated descriptor slots, a descriptor-derived row-level pathology severity, specimen characteristics, staging, biomarkers, margins, and nodal observations share the wide finding-oriented table.

claims.statement: Procedure-level information is a reliable internal V2 surface: within a patient, each complete procedure-date, procedure-type, and biopsy-side tuple identifies one unique procedure, and repeated finding rows can attach several such procedures to one finding.
caveats: Finding side and biopsy side can differ and retain distinct roles.
The tuple is release scoped, incomplete when any component is absent, and not a durable cross-release procedure identifier.
No universal one-to-one pathology attachment is established.

claims.statement: Internal MagView contains columns labeled as specimen, staging, biomarker, margin, and nodal information, but available evidence does not establish that specimen-level representation is present reliably or completely enough for specimen-level operations.
caveats: Do not rely on the specimen number or specimen-associated fields as a complete specimen representation.
No complete durable specimen identity, specimen cardinality, or specimen-collection timestamp is established.

claims.statement: Internal path_severity is produced by the EMBED extraction through a fixed mapping from the path1 through path10 descriptor slots to pathology-type groups, selecting the most severe mapped pathology group linked to the finding and projecting that inverse-severity value onto the finding/procedure association row.
caveats: The occurrence is not a supplied reduction across every procedure row linked to a finding.
A null severity alongside any populated path1 through path10 descriptor is a data-quality error rather than a supported attachment state.

claims.statement: Internal pathology severity value 6 is invalid, has no expected clinical meaning, and is not a historical internal category; the governed internal scale is the canonical 0-through-5 vocabulary.
caveats: Exclude or explicitly flag code 6 as invalid data rather than ordering or grouping it clinically.
Null remains the separate unattached-pathology state.

claims.statement: Historical public documentation assigns classic severity code 5 to negative or normal tissue and code 6 to non-breast cancer, while internal maintainer knowledge and descriptor associations establish code 5 as non-breast cancer and code 6 as invalid with no expected meaning.
caveats: Code 5 is the supported non-breast-cancer category.
Code 6 must not be normalized into any clinical severity category.

claims.statement: The internal MagView table supplies finding-associated path_severity but no side-, exam-, or patient-level pathology-severity aggregate columns.
caveats: Open V2 aggregate bindings must not be copied into this profile.

claims.statement: A downstream exam- or patient-level most-severe reduction is analyst defined: it must declare grouping and attribution and select the minimum represented severity because lower scores are more severe.
caveats: This is not a supplied internal feature, executable workflow, or universal default.
Null severity with any populated descriptor and code 6 are data-quality errors rather than values to order silently.

claims.statement: Both comparison dictionaries label tnmpn as regional-node TNM but attach the primary-tumor code list, while internal tnmpn uses distinct pN-like source tokens.
caveats: The physical occurrence remains mapped as unresolved; no pN code meanings are guessed.
Physical co-location does not establish a unique specimen, procedure, diagnosis, or contemporaneous availability.
The profile records representation and uncertainty rather than an outcome-labeling workflow.

internal-v2.magview-coded-values-context.title: Internal V2 MagView categorical and exceptional-value reconciliation
internal-v2.magview-coded-values-context.summary: Most legacy categorical systems retain V1/V2 meanings, while internal source strings also contain undocumented codes, formatting variants, and unresolved numeric exceptions.

claims.statement: Internal V2 feature codes retain their historical MagView meanings unless a profile-specific claim explicitly supersedes or invalidates a meaning.
caveats: The comparison dictionaries do not establish exhaustive internal domains.
Profile-local vocabularies preserve source tokens rather than normalizing them across releases.

claims.statement: All alphabetic internal MagView codes may be compared after trimming surrounding whitespace and uppercasing; normalization does not assign meanings to otherwise unexplained tokens.
caveats: The original source representation remains part of the physical occurrence.
Comma-delimited fields are split on commas; ordering and repetition do not change meaning.

claims.statement: Several internal imaging, recommendation, pathology, and specimen occurrences contain represented source tokens whose meanings or formatting are absent from the comparison dictionaries.
caveats: Unexplained tokens are retained as unresolved rather than guessed or silently normalized.
Known comma-delimited strings may be tokenized without assigning meaning to unexplained component codes.

claims.statement: Finding side and biopsy side both represent left, right, and bilateral codes; in the clinical finding-side occurrence, null is equivalent to bilateral code B, while biopsy-side null remains unknown and finding-side and biopsy-side values can differ.
caveats: Finding-side B and null both project semantically to the left and right breast-side identities rather than creating a third bilateral breast-side identity.
A null biopsy-side value must not be filled from finding side.

claims.statement: Several measurement-like internal occurrences contain negative source representations whose sentinel or missing meanings are undocumented.
caveats: Do not interpret an exceptional representation as a physical measurement until its field-specific meaning is validated.
Observed absence is not evidence that a documented code cannot occur.
Schema nullability does not establish clinical missingness semantics.

internal-v2.magview-temporal-context.title: Internal V2 MagView temporal and availability limits
internal-v2.magview-temporal-context.summary: The table exposes confirmed exam- and procedure-occurrence dates plus a provisional pathology-report date; no specimen-collection or universal availability timestamp is supported.

claims.statement: Internal V2 studydate_anon represents exam occurrence time; this profile-specific maintainer interpretation supersedes historical public classic-table wording that described a corresponding field as report-signing time.
caveats: Exam occurrence does not necessarily mean the acquisition time of any particular image.

claims.statement: Internal V2 procdate_anon represents procedure occurrence time; this profile-specific maintainer interpretation supersedes historical public classic-table wording that described a corresponding field as pathology-result time.
caveats: Do not substitute this procedure event time for pathology-report or specimen-collection time.

claims.statement: Every anonymized date value across EMBED tables and dataset versions uses one consistent patient-specific shift, so absolute dates are not literal while within-patient ordering and time differences remain reliable across the clinical and image-metadata tables.
caveats: The shift does not establish event meaning for an otherwise undocumented date-like column.

claims.statement: Internal V2 age_at_study_anon is derived from the consistently shifted patient birth and study dates; ages 90 years or older are top-coded to 89.
caveats: Repeated age values may still contain ordinary data-quality inconsistencies.

claims.statement: Internal V2 pdate_anon is believed to represent pathology-report documentation time, but this interpretation has lower maintainer confidence and the field is rarely used in current internal workflows.
caveats: Retain this occurrence as ambiguous until its meaning is independently confirmed.

claims.statement: The assessed MagView clinical table has date-like exam, procedure, and pathology-report occurrences but no supported specimen-collection time or universal downstream-availability timestamp.
caveats: Undocumented date-like columns remain unmapped rather than promoted to temporal semantics.

claims.statement: Co-location of imaging, procedure, pathology, and specimen fields in the MagView row does not establish that downstream information was available at imaging time.
caveats: Task-specific availability boundaries remain analyst responsibilities.
Different date meanings must remain separate; missingness is not repaired through coalescing.
No date is designated as a universal diagnosis date.

internal-v2.v1c-metadata-context.title: Internal V1c image-metadata representation
internal-v2.v1c-metadata-context.summary: The internal clinical V2 profile is paired with the most current internal V1c image-metadata artifact, whose rows describe one extracted DICOM image instance each, carry repeated patient and exam projections and serialized region-of-interest collections, and cover every EMBEDv1 exam and patient while remaining narrower than clinical V2.

claims.statement: One internal V1c image-metadata row represents the attributes of one extracted breast-imaging DICOM image instance, with region-of-interest information serialized inside that row.
caveats: The public description of an image-oriented metadata table was confirmed against the internal V1c artifact rather than assumed.
A row is not a region-of-interest row and is not a file inventory entry.

claims.statement: The internal clinical V2 profile is paired with the most current internal V1c image-metadata artifact, which covers the complete EMBEDv1 exam and patient set and is therefore narrower than internal clinical V2.
caveats: The profile remains internal V2 and is not renamed to V1c; the version boundary describes the current metadata artifact and its EMBEDv1 scope.

claims.statement: A clinical V2 exam with no matching internal V1c image-metadata row lies outside current extraction coverage and is not thereby an exam without images.
caveats: Do not derive an image-availability indicator, a no-image cohort, or an exclusion rule from unmatched exams.

claims.statement: The current V1c metadata covers every exam and patient in EMBEDv1 and includes DICOM objects associated with those accessions after the documented secondary-capture and screen-save exclusions.
caveats: Secondary captures and screen saves are excluded except ROI_SS and ROI_SSC images retained solely to enable extraction of radiologist annotations.

claims.statement: The anonymized SOP Instance UID identifies one DICOM image durably within a dataset version and is encoded as the anon_dicom_path filename without the .dcm suffix, even though it is not exported as a separate metadata column.
caveats: Identity is durable only within the applicable dataset version; no cross-version image identity is asserted.
A missing locator likely means anonymization failed before the de-identified DICOM could be saved, so both the file and its exported identity representation are unavailable for that row.
SeriesNumber and InstanceNumber do not replace the SOP Instance UID and do not distinguish every image row within an accession.

claims.statement: The PNG locator columns are legacy EMBEDv1 FFDM conversion outputs, the extraction-category meaning remains unresolved, and has_pix_array is an obsolete, unreliable field that is no longer populated.
caveats: Use the anonymized DICOM files rather than the legacy PNG conversion for current or future work because the conversion can affect downstream behavior and model generalizability.
Do not interpret has_pix_array values or missingness as reliable evidence about pixel-data availability.
The intended meaning of the extraction category remains unknown.

claims.statement: Internal V1c extracted DICOM objects associated with every EMBEDv1 accession, then excluded secondary captures and screen saves except ROI_SS and ROI_SSC annotation images retained solely for ROI extraction; represented source modalities include mammography, ultrasound, and other.
caveats: The extraction boundary is the EMBEDv1 accession set, not internal clinical V2.
ROI_SS and ROI_SSC are annotation-transfer artifacts and are not intended for other image analyses.

claims.statement: Source DICOM modality, the source DICOM image-type attribute, the pipeline-derived image-type classification, view position, and image laterality are separate internal V1c fields with separate meanings.
caveats: The derived classification only separates mammographic acquisition forms and is not a modality field.
The derived two-dimensional class also covers contrast-enhanced, stereotactic, and post-biopsy acquisitions that are separable only through the source DICOM image-type attribute.
Equivalent source image-type tokens also occur under the residual class, so the classification is not exhaustive.

claims.statement: ROI_SS and ROI_SSC are retained secondary screen-capture images containing burned-in radiologist pixel annotations; an annotation-extraction model converted those annotations to coordinates that were transferred to the corresponding original images, and the screen captures are not intended for any other use.
caveats: These pipeline classes describe annotation-transfer artifacts, not primary diagnostic images or a general secondary-capture inventory.
They are one ROI annotation source; other represented ROIs came through other clinical annotation workflows, including direct extraction from annotation DICOM objects without pixel arrays.

claims.statement: ImageLateralityFinal is the reliable internal V1c attribute for determining which breast an image represents; it contains left or right when represented, while the derivation rule and LateralityDeriveFlag meanings remain unknown.
caveats: Image laterality is not automatically the imaging-finding side or the procedure side.
A missing derived image laterality is not bilateral.
The source ImageLaterality and Laterality attributes remain standard DICOM occurrences; no precedence rule is asserted for reconstructing ImageLateralityFinal.

claims.statement: The clinical and image-metadata tables use the same anonymized patient and exam identifier namespaces: empi_anon supports cross-table patient identity and acc_anon supports cross-table exam identity, while both repeat across internal V1c image rows at their patient and exam levels.
caveats: Each accession must associate with exactly one patient; a cross-patient accession association is an invalid data-quality error that must not be retained as a valid identity or linkage association.
The patient identifier may be used both for cross-table patient identity and as a consistency check on an accession route, but it is not part of exam identity.
Repetition across image rows is physical multiplicity, not clinical multiplicity.

claims.statement: Internal V1c study_date_anon represents the same exam event date as clinical studydate_anon and uses the same patient-specific anonymization shift applied to every anonymized EMBED date value.
caveats: The V1c occurrence is text serialized rather than a parsed timestamp.

claims.statement: Columns parsed directly from standard DICOM data elements retain the applicable DICOM element semantics; the DICOM files received no image or acquisition-attribute processing beyond anonymization and sensitive-information redaction.
caveats: Standard element semantics do not establish internal value validity or pixel-data verification.
PatientAge is top-coded to 89, PatientSex is unchanged, anonymized dates use the confirmed patient-specific shift, and sensitive non-identifier/non-date attributes were dropped.

claims.statement: During DICOM anonymization PatientAge was top-coded to 89, PatientSex was not modified, and sensitive non-identifier/non-date attributes were dropped.
caveats: This claim does not enumerate dropped physical attributes or change the confirmed date-shifting and identifier-anonymization rules.

claims.statement: DICOM Burned In Annotation (0028,0301) declares whether the image contains sufficient burned-in annotation to identify the patient and the date the image was acquired; YES and NO are the defined values, and an absent attribute leaves that condition unknown.
caveats: The attribute is a source declaration and is not a verification of the pixel data.
The catalogue does not prescribe exclusion, redaction, or another action based on this attribute.

claims.statement: acquisition_group_id is constructed as {acc_anon}_{ProtocolName with spaces replaced by hyphens}_{ContentTime cast as an integer}; it is stable across reruns and globally unique for simultaneous image-acquisition groups.
caveats: Spaces are replaced only in ProtocolName as part of the documented construction.
The grouping is not a region-of-interest identity or correspondence representation.

claims.statement: During anonymization acc_anon is written to the DICOM AccessionNumber element; the relationship between StudyID and acc_anon is unknown and StudyID is not relied upon internally.
caveats: Do not use StudyID as an exam identity or assume it equals acc_anon.
The profile remains internal V2; the paired image metadata is the most current internal V1c artifact and covers the complete EMBEDv1 exam and patient set.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: Linked accessions identify explicitly linked co-occurring exams in one imaging episode, but no canonical internal episode identity or complete episode construction is established.
caveats: The link can dangle; conflicting values across repeated rows are data-quality errors, and the link must never be interpreted as a prior-or-follow-up exam relationship.
The separate linked-study flag meaning remains unverified.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: The table represents imaging findings through accession-plus-finding-number identity that can occupy multiple physical rows; side is an attribute rather than an identity component.
caveats: The identity is not persistent across accessions and does not uniquely identify a physical row.
Conflicting repeated side values are data-quality errors rather than distinct finding identities.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: Procedure-level information is a reliable internal V2 surface; within a patient, each complete procedure-date, procedure-type, and biopsy-side tuple identifies one unique procedure.
caveats: The tuple is incomplete when any component is absent, is not durable across releases, and does not establish a universal one-to-one pathology attachment.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: Specimen-labeled columns exist, but specimen-level presence, completeness, reliability, identity, and cardinality are not established for internal V2 operations.
caveats: Do not rely on specimen-level fields for current internal V2 operations.
Specimen number is source scoped and can repeat across rows.

internal-v2.qualification.concept.pathol.summary: The internal occurrence reuses the inverse-severity concept for an extraction-derived row-level projection from path1 through path10; code 5 is non-breast cancer, code 6 is invalid, and null requires every descriptor slot to be empty.
caveats: Exclude or explicitly flag code 6 as invalid rather than ordering it clinically.
Do not coerce null into a governed diagnosis group; a populated descriptor alongside null severity is a data-quality error.

internal-v2.qualification.concept.demogr.summary: Every anonymized date value across EMBED tables and dataset versions uses one consistent patient-specific shift, preserving within-patient ordering and time differences while obscuring absolute dates.
caveats: Repeated patient attributes can still vary or contain data-quality errors.

internal-v2.qualification.concept.demogr.summary: Internal age_at_study_anon is derived from consistently shifted birth and study dates, with ages 90 years or older top-coded to 89.
caveats: Repeated values can still contain ordinary data-quality inconsistencies.

internal-v2.qualification.aggregation.pa.summary: The EMBED extraction supplies the most severe mapped inverse-severity group from the row's path1 through path10 descriptors.
caveats: A populated descriptor alongside null severity is a data-quality error, not a supported state to backfill silently.

internal-v2.qualification.aggregation.pa.summary: The physical severity is projected onto each finding/procedure association row; no supplied reduction across all rows linked to one finding is established.
caveats: One finding can carry multiple severity or attachment states across repeated rows.

internal-v2.qualification.aggregation.pa.summary: No internal side-level pathology-severity aggregate feature is supplied.
caveats: Do not copy the Open V2 side aggregate binding.

internal-v2.qualification.aggregation.pa.summary: No internal exam-level pathology-severity aggregate feature is supplied.
caveats: Any minimum reduction is analyst defined, not a supplied internal feature.

internal-v2.qualification.aggregation.pa.summary: No internal patient-level pathology-severity result or longitudinal rollup is supplied.
caveats: Any patient-level minimum requires an explicit grouping, attribution, and time policy.

internal-v2.qualification.temporal_seman.summary: Internal studydate_anon represents exam occurrence time and participates in the consistent patient-specific date shift.
caveats: Exam occurrence does not necessarily identify acquisition time for a particular image.

internal-v2.qualification.temporal_seman.summary: Internal procdate_anon represents procedure occurrence time and participates in the consistent patient-specific date shift.
caveats: Do not substitute this occurrence for pathology-report or specimen-collection time.

internal-v2.qualification.temporal_seman.summary: Internal pdate_anon is believed to represent pathology-report documentation time, but the interpretation remains provisional because maintainer confidence is limited.
caveats: Do not substitute this provisional occurrence for procedure or specimen-collection time.

internal-v2.qualification.temporal_seman.summary: No supported specimen-collection timestamp is bound in the MagView clinical table.
caveats: Do not invent a proxy from another date-like column.

internal-v2.qualification.temporal_seman.summary: No universal downstream information-availability timestamp is bound.
caveats: Wide-row co-location is not evidence of availability at imaging time.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: The image object is bound to internal V1c at one row per extracted DICOM image instance; the anonymized SOP Instance UID in the anon_dicom_path basename provides dataset-version-scoped identity, and DICOM-derived attributes remain distinct from pipeline-derived and legacy fields.
caveats: Coverage is the complete EMBEDv1 exam and patient set and is narrower than internal clinical V2.
A missing anon_dicom_path likely reflects anonymization failure and makes the de-identified file and exported SOP Instance UID representation unavailable.

internal-v2.qualification.clinical_objec.summary: Regions of interest are physically represented as serialized per-image collections on the internal V1c image-metadata table, with a count and positionally aligned coordinate, frame-index, and depth-derivation collections.
caveats: One physical row can carry several regions, so the table is not one row per region and positional order is not region identity.

Coordinates use inclusive [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] bounds in the attached DICOM pixel-array space; curated coordinates are expected in bounds, and residual out-of-bounds coordinates may be safely clipped.
Routine-clinical radiologist annotations were obtained through multiple workflows, including annotation DICOM objects without pixel arrays and ROI_SS/ROI_SSC screen captures.
Stable per-region identity, cross-image correspondence, and multi-finding attribution remain unsupported.

internal-v2.qualification.semantic_relat.summary: The exam-to-image relationship is physically bound between the internal MagView clinical table and the internal V1c image-metadata extraction through the accession, with physical many-to-many cardinality and incomplete V1c coverage of clinical V2 exams.
caveats: A clinical V2 exam can have no matching V1c image row, and an unmatched exam is not an exam without images.
An inner join on the accession discards clinical V2 exams outside V1c coverage.
Physical linkage does not establish image availability for all internal V2 exams.
